text:
Priya K: Hey team — seeing nondeterministic evals for the new quantized model (redwood-alpha-7q-8bit) when top_p sampling is enabled. Fails ~1/6 runs on CI with different outputs for the same seed. Anyone seen this pattern?
Jamie L: I noticed similar in local runs. Same prompt + seed -> different tokens on rerun. Repro command:
```bash
./eval-runner --model redwood-alpha-7q-8bit --seed 1337 --sampling 'top_p=0.92,temp=0.7' --batch-size 8 --worker-pool=4
```
Jamie L: CI logs show outputs diverge after token 5, checksums mismatch.
Alex M: Two quick hypotheses: 1) PRNG is shared or mis-seeded across worker threads, 2) quantization changed logits precision so borderline top_p selections flip with tiny numeric jitter.
Rachel S: FWIW temp=0.0 + top_p disabled is fully deterministic for me. The flake only shows up when top_p>0 and multiple workers are active.
Priya K: Good call. I captured a minimal trace — when we resume a stopped batch the rng_cursor values look different across workers. Snippet from worker debug:
```txt
[worker-2] rng_cursor=1024 seed_base=1337
[worker-3] rng_cursor=1016 seed_base=1337
```
Priya K: Those cursor deltas shouldn't happen for identical inputs.
Alex M: That suggests RNG state is being advanced by other actors (batch coalescing / prefix caching) before a worker handles a sample. Could be a global rng instance used for scheduling decisions.
Jamie L: Also noticed in quantized runs the softmax logits for the top candidates have smaller margins. top_p relies on cumulative probs; tiny reordering due to interleaving can change which token crosses the threshold.
Rachel S: Repro case I used: single prompt repeated in 128-example batch with resume on worker 3. Interleaving order changed sampling calls sequence.
Priya K: Proposed fixes: (1) enforce per-worker PRNG seeded with hash(seed, worker_id) and use deterministic consume pattern, (2) add a sampling lock or deterministic scheduling mode for eval CI, (3) add a checksum test that runs 20 seeds in CI with quantized config.
Alex M: I'll open a small PR to initialize RNGs per worker and replace any global RandomState usage in runner. Also add a --deterministic-scheduler flag that forces single-threaded sampling order for CI.
Jamie L: For the quantization angle, we should add a numerical stability test: run float32 vs quantized logits softmax/stable-softmax diff stats, and fail if median L1 > 1e-6 for top-k.
Priya K: Sounds good. Can we also add telemetry to record (seed, worker_id, rng_cursor) per sample to help postmortem if this recurs?
Rachel S: yes, lightweight logs to S3 or local artifact would help. Also add a note in the eval-runner docs about sampling determinism caveats with top_p+quantization.
eval-bot: CI check 'eval-repro-smoke' failed on commit abc123 — rerun link: https://ci.redwood/example/3321
Priya K: I'll file the follow-ups: 1) PR for per-worker RNG (Alex), 2) CI deterministic job + checksums (Jamie), 3) quant softmax diagnostic job (Rachel). Assigning now.
Jamie L: I'll add the CI job and checksum harness today. :thumbsup:
Alex M: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/456 — implements per-worker RNG + --deterministic-scheduler. PTAL.
Rachel S: Running 50 seeds locally against PR456 — initially no flakes in 200 runs. Looks promising.
Priya K: Great. Leave this thread open until CI green on the repro job. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
